findings.title: Escalation path can itself raise on a malformed run id
findings.description: `_in_flight_run_ids` reads `entry.parameters[PARAM_RUN_ID]` with a hard subscript and wraps it in `str()`. `RunObserver._observe_one` and `finish._run_id` both raise `ValueError` when the run id is missing, empty or not a string. The tenant's process-boundary catch then calls `escalate`, which reaches `_in_flight_run_ids` for that same entry. If the run id is absent, that raises `KeyError` inside the `except` handler, and the process dies instead of escalating. If the run id is not a string, `str()` hides the bad value. The comment in `tenant.py` ("a failing escalation write means a broken store") is then wrong. Use `.get` and skip or report entries whose run id is unusable.

findings.title: Run-id extraction is duplicated in three places
findings.description: The same "read `PARAM_RUN_ID`, require a non-empty string" logic appears in `observe._observe_one`, `finish._run_id` and `faults._in_flight_run_ids`. `launch._text_parameter` is a fourth variant. The copies already disagree: the first two raise `ValueError`, and the third subscripts and calls `str()`. This breaks the project's DRY rule, and it is the cause of the finding above. Define one accessor (for example in `launch.py` or the store models) and use it everywhere.

findings.title: `observe.py` exceeds the size guideline
findings.description: The file is about 326 lines against the ~300-line guideline. The unconfirmed-launch logic (`_unconfirmed`, `_check_line`, `_after_launch_poll`, `_still_overdue`) is a self-contained state machine. It could move to its own module, which would also shrink the long argument lists those methods pass around.

findings.title: Test code weakens strict typing and patches global state
findings.description: The rules include tests in strict pyright. `_hooked` returns `tuple[object, object]` and is then fed to `RunnerTenant` through `# type: ignore[arg-type]` on both values. `_arm_resolve_kill` replaces `Store.journal_resolve` on the class with `# type: ignore[method-assign]`. Other test files add `Any` and `type: ignore` too: `ScriptedPoll.on_call`, `Rig.launch(e: object)` with an `assert isinstance`, and the `make_rig: Any` fixture. Return a typed `NamedTuple` or `Protocol` pair from `_hooked`. Give the support rigs real types instead of `Any`.

findings.title: Source-text assertion for the single broad `except`
findings.description: This test counts occurrences of the string `except Exception` in the package source. It is a brittle guard: a comment or docstring containing that phrase breaks it, and a differently written broad catch, such as `except BaseException`, passes it. The `BLE` ruff rule already enforces this mechanically, so the test adds little.

findings.title: Mutable-looking constant lacks `Final`
findings.description: `CLOSED_BY: str = "runner"` is annotated `str` while every other module constant in the package uses `Final`. `tenant.py` also defines `RUNNER_TENANT_NAME` with the same value. Use `Final` and share one definition.

findings.title: Possible long line on the `noqa` comment
findings.description: The line `except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - the Runner's one process boundary (D8)` looks longer than 88 characters. Ruff E501 would flag it unless the project config ignores it. I could not run ruff to confirm.

findings.title: Design, safety and test coverage
findings.description:
The following held up on reading:
- **Tick budget:** it is checked before every subprocess call, including `Popen`, and `test_budget_coverage.py` guards against new call sites that skip it.
- **Launch ordering:** the journal entry is written before the launch, with the block-then-resolve ordering made idempotent.
- **Exception handling:** the broad catch is a documented process-boundary handler that re-raises store failures and upstream shape errors.
- **Detached children:** logs are created exclusively, children get their own session, and failures are recorded.
- **Crash recovery:** SIGKILL tests cover four kill points.
- **Database safety:** tests use throwaway stores and never read a production URL.
- **Import boundaries:** rules 10 and 11 are enforced by tests.

structured_findings.summary: Escalation path can itself raise on a malformed run id
Run-id extraction is duplicated in three places
Test code weakens strict typing and patches global state
Source-text assertion for the single broad `except`
Possible long line on the `noqa` comment
